research_lane: five uploaded Jyotish books; source-only not participant data

evidence_access.encoding_caveat: PDF Sanskrit glyph OCR is poor; rely on English source text and keep original-language parse open

source.edition: J. N. Bhasin English translation scanned 374-page user Library PDF
source.verification: file-library text extraction read at source PDF pages; page images did not return as pixels, so Sanskrit glyph recognition is NOT independently verified

collations.source_locator: Sarvārtha Cintāmaṇi Ch6 v58, physical PDF p172/374
collations.bhasin_gloss: Rahu or Ketu in the seventh, with malefic aspect and cruel navamsa; historical hostile allegations about wife's conduct
collations.alternative_online_gloss: Rahu and Ketu in seventh; literal impossible co-occupation
collations.editorial_conclusion: Printed Bhasin explicitly reads OR, while the online explanation says AND. The antipodal node geometry refutes only the literal same-seventh AND interpretation, not the classical condition as translated by Bhasin. Morphology/edition variation not proven.
collations.human_ethics: Never issue allegations of infidelity/poisoning/violence against any spouse on an astrological rule; document only as source history.

collations.bhasin_gloss: Rise in fortune/prospects happens a long time after marriage under stated malefic configurations
collations.editorial_conclusion: Two translations favor DELAY IN POSTMARRIAGE PROSPERITY, not DELAY TO FIRST MARRIAGE; do not operationalize as marriage-age predictor.

collations.bhasin_gloss: Extend method to early/late acquisition of sons; Bhasin adds explanatory observation that malefic influences delay.
collations.editorial_conclusion: The English print explicitly names children acquisition timing; verify Sanskrit before attributing the malefic-delay gloss to original author instead of translator.

collations.bhasin_gloss: Bālye marriage described as early boyhood/childhood, with additional ascendant/seventh/second and strong division conditions
collations.editorial_conclusion: The wording indicates childhood, not a generic early 20s marriage; do not update a contemporary behavioral questionnaire to normalize child marriage.

collations.bhasin_gloss: Postmarital improvement (v62), financial deterioration (v63), later recovery after loss (v64) under differing configurations
collations.editorial_conclusion: Three conditional states, not three independent corroborations for one financial trajectory; cannot count a loss-and-recovery as a single net 'prosperity' prediction.

supersessions.scope: The assertion that the historical Bhasin passage itself requires both nodes in the 7th
supersessions.preserved: The 12/12 nodal antipodal geometry test remains correct given the literal joint-conjunction premise, but Bhasin writes OR; must keep alternative parse open.

supersessions.scope: Referent 'late fortune or late marriage' unresolved at the English-translation level
supersessions.preserved: Both print Bhasin and online English read late improvement AFTER marriage. Independent Sanskrit grammatical adjudication and precise operational timing remain open.

supersessions.scope: Parenthood timing treated as only a generic method transfer
supersessions.preserved: Bhasin explicitly claims early/late attainment of sons; separate translator's malefic-delay explanation from literal Sanskrit.
